transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to focus today's call on the quality evaluation plan for the POC — golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination checks, scoring approach, and timeline. quick intros?
[00:12] Dr. Elena: hi, elena here, CMIO. main goal is to make sure any clinical outputs are safe and formatted for our downstream EHR ingest.
[00:20] Ravi: ravi - head of data. i'll be owning the dataset side and sample extraction. we've got PHI concerns so we'll need redaction and KMS rules.
[00:28] Sasha: sasha, eng mgr, i'll coordinate infra and api integration.
[00:34] Jordan: thanks. priya from our SE team will lead the eval harness. priya?
[00:38] Priya: hey all. quick note - i'll propose a concrete scoring rubric and baseline scripts. will also handle the benchmark runs.
[00:46] Jordan: cool. first, success criteria. elena, what does success look like for you at the end of the POC?
[00:52] Dr. Elena: we need two things: clinical correctness (i.e., no dangerous hallucinations) and strict format compliance so the EHR can parse without manual fixes. ideally we want >95% format pass and <5% hallucination rate on the golden set.
[01:06] Ravi: add to that cost/latency targets; we want p95 latency <750ms for summary responses at ~512 tokens, and throughput to handle our peak of ~120 requests/min during business hours.
[01:18] Jordan: good — we'll include p95 latency and throughput in the benchmark. for quality eval plan, our proposal: 1) golden prompts (50-100 canonical examples), 2) regression suite (500 representative prompts sampled from prod patterns), 3) automated checks for hallucination/factuality, 4) strict format validation (JSON schema), and 5) scoring combining schema pass, semantic similarity, and clinical correctness adjudication. sound aligned?
[01:42] Dr. Elena: yes. can you clarify "automated hallucination checks"? how do you detect hallucinations reliably?
[01:48] Priya: good q. automated checks will use a mix: 1) entity extraction + cross-check against provided EHR fields (e.g., medication names, lab values), 2) citation/linking heuristics for cases where model must reference notes, and 3) semantic similarity thresholds to golden answers. anything ambiguous will be flagged for SME review. automated step is a filter, not final.
[02:10] Ravi: will you run LLM-based factuality classifiers? we tried something that flagged too many false positives.
[02:15] Priya: yes we'll combine classifiers with rule-based checks to reduce false positives; also we'll calibrate thresholds using the golden set.
[02:23] Jordan: for scoring, proposed weights: format/schema pass 40%, semantic similarity (embedding cosine / rouge) 30%, clinical SME pass 30%. pass threshold overall 85% to be considered acceptable. format must be >=95% independently.
[02:36] Dr. Elena: SME pass 30% seems low — clinical safety is priority. can we make SME pass a hard gate for certain categories (e.g., medication changes, dosing recommendations)?
[02:46] Priya: absolutely. we can flag high-risk categories where SME approval is required regardless of overall score. we'll capture category labels in the prompt metadata.
[02:54] Sasha: on format, we require a strict JSON schema: fields for code (LOINC/SNOMED), short_summary, actions_needed (list), confidence_score (0-1). the model must output valid JSON. does redwood have schema-enforcement tooling we can plug into the harness?
[03:07] Jordan: yes — Redwood's structured output support includes schema validation and structured output retries; we'll hook that into the harness and report pass/fail counts. note: transcription sometimes mislabels redwood product names as "Redwood Verify" etc, but feature exists.
[03:20] Ravi: workload sizing: we expect average tokens per request ~350 for summaries, with tail up to 1500 for long notes. daily traffic for POC will be modest ~10k requests/day, but we want the POC to simulate peak bursts of 5x.
[03:34] Priya: okay we'll set traffic generator to replay 500 sample prompts/minute bursts to simulate peaks. also will include a long-tail bucket for 5% of requests at 1500 tokens.
[03:44] Jordan: benchmarks to run week 2: cold-start latency, steady-state p50/p95/p99, throughput with KV caching enabled vs disabled, quality vs quantized model variants. we'll capture token cost estimates.
[03:56] Dr. Elena: can we include hallucination spot checks specifically around medication dosing and allergies? those are critical.
[04:02] Priya: yes — we'll create a tagged subset of golden prompts for meds/allergies and require SME review on those.
[04:08] Ravi: about data handling — we need VPC connectivity and customer-managed KMS. does Redwood's private deployment support customer KMS/HSM on the POC?
[04:16] Jordan: yes we can run the POC in a VPC with customer KMS for enterprise/private options; for hosted we offer envelope encryption but for Community Health we recommend VPC. we'll attach the security pack in the next email.
[04:28] Sasha: timing — what is typical POC duration and cadence?
[04:31] Jordan: typical is 4 weeks: week 0 (kickoff + infra), week 1 (dataset ingestion & golden prompt finalization), week 2 (baseline benchmarks + quality runs), week 3 (iterate on model/config, run regression suite), week 4 (final scoring, presentation & decision).
[04:48] Priya: on the eval harness itself — we'll provide a baseline python harness that runs prompts, validates schema, computes embedding-based similarity scores, runs our hallucination heuristics, and exports a CSV for SME review. it uses deterministic seeding for reproducibility.
[05:03] Ravi: what about model variants? we want to test both hosted small/med models and a dedicated quantized variant — plus a fallback plan.
[05:11] Priya: we'll test three model families: a higher-quality ~base LLM (hosted), a quantized dedicated variant for cost tests, and a lower-cost fast model for latency comparisons. the harness will label outputs with model id and quantization profile.
[05:25] Dr. Elena: scoring detail: for semantic similarity what metric do you use? cosine on sentence embeddings?
[05:30] Priya: we'll compute both embedding cosine (SBERT-style embeddings) and rouge-l/meteor as additional signals; final similarity score is a weighted combo tuned on the golden set.
[05:40] Sasha: on regression tests — how do you prevent data leakage if we use real patient examples?
[05:46] Ravi: we'll anonymize and de-identify, and provide synthetic variants for public artifacts.
[05:50] Priya: also the harness supports mapping prompts to categories so we can ensure coverage across templates and not overfit to the golden set.
[05:58] Jordan: acceptance criteria recap: 1) overall score >=85%, 2) format/schema pass >=95%, 3) hallucination rate <=5% on golden meds/allergy subset, 4) p95 latency <=750ms for 512-token baseline, 5) cost estimate within agreed threshold.
[06:17] Dr. Elena: who does the final clinical adjudication?
[06:19] Jordan: you'll nominate an SME (elena or someone on your side) and we'll provide an adjudication sheet for easy review; Redwood can optionally provide a clinical reviewer for an extra fee but for POC initial SME should come from customer.
[06:33] Ravi: reporting — will we get dashboarding and per-prompt breakdowns?
[06:36] Priya: yes the Redwood Console will show per-model/per-route metrics and we will deliver a quality report with per-prompt scores, failed examples, and recommended mitigations.
[06:46] Sasha: any blockers on our side? we need to confirm VPC peering details and legal for data transfer.
[06:52] Jordan: we'll put those in the action items. i'll send legal and security docs.
[06:56] Dr. Elena: ok, one more question — regression pass/fail thresholds: do you allow incremental rollouts based on quality gates?
[07:03] Priya: yes — Redwood supports canary rollouts and automatic fallback when quality or latency thresholds are breached. we'll show a canary config as part of the recommendations. note: sometimes the runtime calls it "routing policy" in the console, transcription sometimes munges names.
[07:19] Ravi: for the golden prompts, we propose 50 core examples across categories: summaries, triage, med reconciliation, discharge instructions. we'll create these and send.
[07:28] Jordan: perfect. i'll put a template for golden prompts in the doc i share. it includes expected JSON fields, allowed values for codes, and example SME decisions.
[07:37] Dr. Elena: are there recommended thresholds for embedding similarity? we need guidance to calibrate.
[07:42] Priya: as a starting point we'll use cosine >=0.82 as probable match, 0.75-0.82 as review-needed, <0.75 likely fail — we'll tune on your golden set.
[07:54] Jordan: timeline recap and next steps: jordan sends security pack by 4/2; ravi sends prompts by 4/6; priya kicks off infra week of 4/6; baseline demo 4/13; final scoring and review week of 5/4.
[08:09] Sasha: ok thanks, that works. any other questions?
[08:12] Dr. Elena: none from me. thanks.
[08:15] Jordan: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with an email with attachments and meeting notes.
[08:20] Priya: action items in the doc; i'll set up the first harness run once we have the prompts.
[08:25] Jordan: cool — meeting adjourned.
